comparison: Both evaluate foundational claims about BRAIN Initiative origins and structure (C1-C5). OpenEval provides detailed assessment of historical facts and governance, while peer reviewers accept these as 'convincing summary' without specific critique. Both find claims SUPPORTED.

Both address conceptual framework claims (C6-C9). OpenEval notes the logical progression but flags C9's 'all brain disorders' as strong generalization. Peer reviewers accept framework as part of convincing description without questioning the generalization. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate BRAIN-NIH relationship claims (C10-C11). OpenEval acknowledges evaluative nature but accepts based on organizational structure. Peer reviewers accept without critique as part of program documentation. Both SUPPORTED.
Both address organizational structure claims (C12-C16). OpenEval treats as verifiable administrative facts. Peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive program description. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate strategic focus claims (C17-C23). OpenEval notes citations and clearly stated program features. Peer reviewers accept as part of convincing documentation allowing readers to 'parse what this BRAIN program funded.' Both SUPPORTED.

Both address funding structure claims (C24-C30). OpenEval emphasizes citations and documented program features. Peer reviewers describe as 'fair bit of documentation' of 'specific funding mechanisms.' Both accept quantitative data without challenge. Both SUPPORTED.
Both evaluate quantitative funding data (C31-C34). OpenEval notes support from Figure 1B and verifiability from financial records. Peer reviewers accept as factual documentation. Both SUPPORTED.
Both address TMM program claims (C35-C42). OpenEval details documented program features distinguishing TMM from other funding. Peer reviewers note documentation of program outputs. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate tool impact assessment (C43-C46). OpenEval acknowledges GitHub metrics represent only one dimension of impact. Peer reviewers accept analyses of 'popularity of some tools developed' as part of documentation. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C47-C53). Both evaluate newly launched program with premature impact assessment. OpenEval explicitly notes acknowledgment that assessment is premature. Peer reviewers accept as program structure documentation. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C54-C57). Both address funding growth rates. OpenEval notes C57's inference relies on assumptions. Peer reviewers describe as 'analyses of the impact on overall funding' and note 'improved presentation.' Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate bibliometric measures (C58-C66). OpenEval notes standard measures requiring careful interpretation of limitations. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'analyses of...raw and field normalized bibliographic impact' as part of what makes manuscript 'convincing.' Both SUPPORTED.

Both address comparative bibliometric analysis (C67-C73). OpenEval notes evaluative terms lack statistical testing. Peer reviewers accept as straightforward data interpretations strengthening manuscript. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate publication/citation accumulation (C74-C76). OpenEval acknowledges 'healthy' is subjective but data support assessment. Peer reviewers accept as part of convincing bibliometric documentation. Both SUPPORTED.
Both address advancement rates (C77-C81). OpenEval notes rates substantially higher than typical NIH success rates. Peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive documentation. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate limitations acknowledgment (C86-C88). OpenEval treats as important caveat about metric limitations. Peer reviewers implicitly accept by not challenging, appreciating scientific caution. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C89-C97). Both address public impact via Altmetric scores. OpenEval notes diversity demonstrates broad public interest. Peer reviewers note 'analyses of...social media impact' as appropriate documentation. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C98-C105). Both evaluate team-research program history and finances. OpenEval emphasizes well-documented evolution. Peer reviewers note authors 'draw on wealth of real-life experience' with team projects. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address consortium activities (C106-C109). OpenEval notes visual evidence from topic maps. Peer reviewers accept as part of authors' documented experience with program management. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate advancement data and strategy effectiveness (C110-C116). OpenEval concludes substantially higher rates support effectiveness. Peer reviewers accept as evidence of program success without questioning interpretation. Both SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates team consolidation metric (C117) as meaningful despite small sample. Peer reviewers group with broader advancement data (R10) accepting as part of team-science effectiveness evidence. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address cultural impact via survey data (C118-C124). OpenEval notes limitation to meeting attendees. Peer reviewers accept survey evidence as demonstrating program's influence on research practices. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate consortium collaborative activities (C125-C129). OpenEval treats as documented activities extending beyond individual awards. Peer reviewers accept as part of convincing cultural impact documentation. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address training benefits and challenges (C130-C139). OpenEval notes balanced assessment with citations. Peer reviewers accept acknowledgment of challenges alongside successes as adding credibility. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate BRAIN influence on other NIH programs (C140-C141). OpenEval treats as concrete example of impact beyond direct funding. Peer reviewers accept as part of program documentation. Both SUPPORTED.

High claim overlap (C142-C147). Both address data science core effectiveness. OpenEval notes balanced assessment from site visits and self-evaluation. Peer reviewers accept balanced assessment of successes and improvement areas. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C148-C151). Both evaluate site visit process and value. OpenEval acknowledges evaluative nature but notes documented features. Peer reviewers accept based on authors' documented experience. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address model system diversity (C152-C154). OpenEval notes verifiable species list and reasonable inference about mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept as evidence of program breadth. Both SUPPORTED.
Both evaluate quantitative integration impact (C155-C157). OpenEval notes assessment based on program experience. Peer reviewers accept as part of convincing scope documentation. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address workforce development (C158-C162). OpenEval notes survey provides quantitative evidence but uncertain generalizability. Peer reviewers accept survey data as demonstrating training influence. Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate team science review framework (C163-C169). OpenEval treats as documented program features with citation. Peer reviewers describe manuscript as 'convincing' and note clarity improvements. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address conclusions and recommendations (C170-C174). OpenEval acknowledges evaluative nature but notes support from extensive data. Peer reviewers accept as reasonable conclusions, characterizing as 'important summary.' Both SUPPORTED.

Both evaluate overall conclusions (C175-C179). OpenEval notes support from extensive quantitative/qualitative data. Peer reviewers characterize as 'convincing' and 'of particular value at this moment in history.' Both SUPPORTED.

Both address summary conclusions (C180-C183). OpenEval notes documented investment and growth with bibliometric support. Peer reviewers accept magnitude and significance of claimed impacts without challenge. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect claim overlap (C184-C186). Both evaluate methodology descriptions. OpenEval notes scripts not publicly available for verification. Peer reviewers accept methodological transparency as appropriate without questioning validity. Both SUPPORTED.
